'''Tony LaShae Mitchell Jr.'''<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.nba.com/pistons/sites/pistons/files/mg_1415_players.pdf |title=2014–15 Detroit Pistons Media Guide |page=48 |work=NBA.com |accessdate=May 6, 2022}}</ref> (born April 7, 1992) is an American professional [[basketball]] player who last played for the [[Macau Black Knights]] of the [[Philippine Basketball Association]] (PBA). He competed in college for [[North Texas Mean Green men's basketball|North Texas]].<ref name=STAR>{{cite web| last =Henry| first =John| title =North Texas star Tony Mitchell's journey could lead to NBA| work =[[Fort Worth Star-Telegram]]| publisher =[[The McClatchy Company]]| date =November 27, 2012| url =http://www.star-telegram.com/2012/11/27/4443331/north-texas-star-tony-mitchells.html| access-date = February 8, 2013}}</ref> Mitchell is {{height|ft=6|in=7}}, weighs 235 pounds and plays the [[power forward]] position.<ref name=nbaprofile>{{cite web | title=Tony Mitchell Stats, Bio and Game Logs | work=NBA.com | url=http://www.nba.com/playerfile/tony_l_mitchell/ | access-date=September 5, 2013}}</ref> Mitchell was selected in the [[2013 NBA draft]] in the second round (37th pick overall).

==High school career==
Mitchell played three years of prep basketball.<ref name=USAB>{{cite web|title=USA Basketball: Tony Mitchell |work=USABasketball.com |publisher=NBA Media Ventures, LLC |date=June 2011 |url=http://www.usabasketball.com/bios/mitchell_tony.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100706192921/http://www.usabasketball.com/bios/mitchell_tony.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=July 6, 2010 |access-date=February 8, 2013 }}</ref> For his career, he posted over 1,500 [[point (basketball)|points]] and 700 [[rebound (basketball)|rebounds]].<ref name=USAB/> As a [[senior (education)|senior]] at [[L. G. Pinkston High School]] he averaged 20.5 points, 13.2 rebounds, 4.4 [[assist (basketball)|assists]] and 4.1 [[block (basketball)|blocks]] per game while leading his school to a 26–10 record and a berth in the Class 4A Region II Tournament.<ref name=UNT>{{cite web | title =Tony Mitchell – North Texas Mean Green | work =MeanGreenSports.com | publisher =[[University of North Texas]] | year =2012 | url =http://www.meangreensports.com/ViewArticle.dbml?SPSID=9109&SPID=564&DB_LANG=C&DB_OEM_ID=1800&ATCLID=205320061&Q_SEASON=2012 | access-date =February 8, 2013 | url-status =dead | archive-url =https://web.archive.org/web/20130621113731/http://www.meangreensports.com/ViewArticle.dbml?SPSID=9109&SPID=564&DB_LANG=C&DB_OEM_ID=1800&ATCLID=205320061&Q_SEASON=2012 | archive-date =June 21, 2013 }}</ref> In one playoff game against [[Lincoln High School (Dallas)|Lincoln High School]] he recorded 25 points, 20 rebounds and five blocks in an [[overtime (sports)|overtime]] win.<ref name=UNT/> Mitchell was ranked as the #12 overall senior recruit in the class of 2010 by [[Rivals.com]].<ref name=UNT/><ref name=SI/> His accolades also included being named the 2010 ''[[Dallas Morning News]]'' Player of the Year – beating out [[Perry Jones III]], a future first round NBA Draft pick out of [[Baylor Bears basketball|Baylor]]; a ''[[SLAM Magazine]]'' All-American; Texas' 12-4A Player of the Year; Texas Class 4A All-State selection; and being chosen to the Texas Association of Basketball Coaches All-Star Team.<ref name=USAB/><ref name=UNT/>

===NCAA eligibility issues===
Mitchell attended a public high school in Atlanta (Dutchtown High School) for his [[freshman]] year then in Dallas sophomore years, but under the advice of his [[Amateur Athletic Union]] basketball coach he transferred to Center of Life Christian Academy (CLCA) in Miami.<ref name=SI>{{cite magazine| last =Winn| first =Luke| title =Ex-Mizzou recruit Mitchell ready to make comeback at North Texas | magazine =[[Sports Illustrated]]| publisher =CNN/SI| date =July 21, 2011| url =http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/2011/writers/luke_winn/07/18/Tony.Mitchell/index.html| archive-url =https://web.archive.org/web/20110810192726/http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/2011/writers/luke_winn/07/18/Tony.Mitchell/index.html| url-status =dead| archive-date =August 10, 2011| access-date = February 8, 2013}}</ref> What he did not realize until the latter portion of his [[Junior (education year)|junior]] year there, however, was that CLCA was not an accredited prep school, and therefore only a fraction of his coursework counted toward [[National Collegiate Athletic Association|NCAA]] eligibility.<ref name=SI/> Mitchell transferred back home to Pinkston to finish his prep career.<ref name=SI/> To make up for lost time at CLCA, he attempted to take make-up classes at a faster rate than the school district allowed.<ref name=SI/> After an investigation into his course load, and upon discovering Mitchell's attempted expedition of his graduation requirements, his transcript got invalidated and his high school graduation was postponed while he struggled with Texas' exit test.<ref name=SI/>

Mitchell had already committed to play for the [[Missouri Tigers men's basketball|Missouri Tigers]] while these issues unfolded.<ref name=SI/> Forced to stay at home in Dallas for the entire first semester of what would have been his freshman year playing for Missouri, it was not until the start of the second semester when he found out that he would never be allowed to suit up for the Tigers.<ref name=SI/> Mitchell then had to choose one of two routes: either play [[Junior college#Athletics|junior college]] basketball for two seasons, or play for a different four-year institution as a partial qualifier.<ref name=SI/> He chose to play as a partial qualifier for [[North Texas Mean Green men's basketball|North Texas]], the local [[Division I (NCAA)|Division I]] school whose coach, [[Johnny Jones (basketball, born 1961)|Johnny Jones]], had aggressively recruited him during his high school years.<ref name=SI/>

==College career==

===Freshman season===
After sitting out the [[2010–11 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2010–11 season]] due to his eligibility issues, Mitchell officially began his collegiate career as a [[redshirt (sports)|redshirt]] freshman in [[2011–12 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2011–12]].<ref name=UNT/><ref name=SI/> He quickly established himself as a premier player in both the Sun Belt Conference as well as nationally; Mitchell was named by [[CBS Sports]] as one of the "top 10 freshmen in the country" and their third-best "under the radar" player after averaging 14.7 points and 10.3 rebounds per game.<ref name=UNT/> Along with [[2011–12 Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball team|Kentucky]]'s [[Anthony Davis]], he was one of only two freshmen in NCAA Division I to average a [[double-double]] (Davis was also that season's national player of the year and the [[List of first overall NBA draft picks|first overall draft pick]] in the [[2012 NBA draft|ensuing NBA draft]]).<ref name=UNT/><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/draft/|title=Draft Index|access-date=February 10, 2013|publisher=Sports Reference LLC|work=basketball-reference.com|year=2012}}</ref> Among freshmen, only Davis' 10.4 rebounds per game average exceeded Mitchell's.<ref name=UNT/> He set school records for single season blocks (70) and blocks per game (3.04), while his single game top scoring and rebounding performances were 34 and 21, respectively.<ref name=UNT/> Despite the team not qualifying for any postseason tournaments, Mitchell still received awards and honors for his personal play. He became just the second player in league history to earn three consecutive Sun Belt Player of the Week awards while also becoming just the third player to be named the league's freshman of the year and earn a first team all-conference selection simultaneously.<ref name=UNT/> Mitchell was named to the All-[[2012 Sun Belt Conference men's basketball tournament|2012 Sun Belt Conference tournament]] team after leading the Mean Green to the championship game before losing to [[2011–12 WKU Hilltoppers basketball team|Western Kentucky]], 74 to 70.<ref name=UNT/> According to his North Texas player page, "In league-only games, Mitchell led the Sun Belt in scoring (15.9 ppg), rebounding (11.8 rpg), 3-point percentage (47.1), blocks (3.1 bpg), and was also second in field goal percentage (58.1)."<ref name=UNT/> Mitchell had numerous 30-point, 15-rebound games during the season and became the first freshman since [[Kansas State Wildcats men's basketball|Kansas State]]'s [[Michael Beasley]] in [[2007–08 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2007–08]] to record multiple 30/15 games.<ref name=UNT/> For his standout season, he was named a finalist for the [[Lou Henson Award]], an annual college basketball award given to the nation's best [[mid-major]] player.<ref name=UNT/>

===Sophomore season===
Heading into his sophomore season in [[2012–13 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2012–13]], national media had their eyes on Mitchell as a potential [[NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|All-American]].<ref name=BR>{{cite web| last =Henry| first =Scott| title =Why Is North Texas' Tony Mitchell Not Playing Like an All-American?| website =Bleacher Report| date =December 24, 2012| url =https://bleacherreport.com/articles/1455713-why-is-north-texas-tony-mitchell-not-playing-like-an-all-american| access-date = February 8, 2013}}</ref> He had been a projected first round draft pick in the [[2012 NBA draft]] following his freshman season,<ref name=USAT>{{cite news| last =Gleeson| first =Scott M.| title =Mid-Major Player Diary: Tony Mitchell doesn't regret NBA decision| newspaper =[[USA Today]]| date =January 8, 2013| url =https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/ncaab/2013/01/08/mid-major-player-diary-tony-mitchell-doesnt-regret-nba-decision/1793449/| access-date = February 8, 2013}}</ref> but opted to remain at North Texas because he said he "still needed to mature on and off the court."<ref name=USAT/> Some of the preseason watchlists and honors that Mitchell received included being an All-American according to numerous media outlets; a [[John Wooden Award]] Preseason Top 50 player; being featured on the October cover of ''[[Basketball Times]]''; Lindy's number two ranked [[center (basketball)|center]] in college basketball; and CBS Sports' number seven overall player in the country.<ref name=UNT/> He was listed as a "near guarantee" to be named the 2013 [[Sun Belt Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year|Sun Belt Player of the Year]] according to CBS Sports.<ref name=PREVIEW>{{cite web|last=Norlander|first=Matt|  title =College Basketball Previews: With NBA-prospect Tony Mitchell, North Texas is favored in Sun Belt| work =CBS Sports| date = October 16, 2012| url =http://www.cbssports.com/collegebasketball/blog/eye-on-college-basketball/20573576/college-basketball-previews-with-nba-prospect-tony-mitchell-north-texas-is-favored-in-sun-belt| access-date = February 8, 2013}}</ref> An anonymous Sun Belt coach said of Mitchell: "[He] is the most athletic guy in college basketball, bar none. Rebounds as good as anyone. He's a freak."<ref name=PREVIEW/>

Mitchell's per-game averages lowered in four of the five major statistical categories from his freshman season: 13.0 points (down from 14.7), 8.5 rebounds (down from 10.3), 0.8 assists (down from 1.6), and 2.7 blocks (down from 3.0).<ref name=SR>{{cite web|title =Tony Mitchell| publisher =Sports Reference LLC| work=sports-reference.com | date =February 11, 2013| url =https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/players/tony-mitchell-4.html| access-date = February 11, 2013}}</ref> Only his steals per game average increased, going from 0.9 as a freshman to 1.0 in his second year.<ref name=SR/> Additionally, the North Texas squad managed just a 12–20 overall record (7–13 in conference) after being selected as the preseason Sun Belt Conference champions.<ref>{{cite web| title =2012–13 North Texas results| publisher =University of North Texas| work =MeanGreenSports.com| date =February 11, 2013| url =http://www.meangreensports.com/SportSelect.dbml?&DB_OEM_ID=1800&SPID=564&SPSID=9108| access-date =February 11, 2013| url-status =dead| archive-url =https://web.archive.org/web/20130131012639/http://www.meangreensports.com/SportSelect.dbml?&DB_OEM_ID=1800&SPID=564&SPSID=9108| archive-date =January 31, 2013}}</ref> Midway through the season, [[Bleacher Report]] wrote an article which questioned Mitchell's ability to lead a team, noting that a player of his caliber should have been a bigger factor in games played in a mid-major conference.<ref name=BR/> The article also said that his All-American candidacy took a severe blow, and that his per game averages would be more impressive if he played for a stronger Division I program.<ref name=BR/>

==Professional career==

===Detroit Pistons (2013–2014)===
With a college postseason invitation not occurring, Mitchell decided to be the first underclassman to declare for the [[2013 NBA draft]]. He was the first North Texas player to be drafted in the NBA since the [[Dallas Mavericks]] drafted John Horrocks in [[1984 NBA draft|1984]].<ref name=UNTDRAFT>{{cite web|title =North Texas NBA Draft Picks|publisher =Mean Green Ball|year =2013|url =http://meangreenball.com/north-texas-basketball/roster_nba_draft|access-date =March 27, 2013|url-status =dead|archive-url =https://archive.today/20130411080813/http://meangreenball.com/north-texas-basketball/roster_nba_draft|archive-date =April 11, 2013}}</ref> Mitchell was drafted by the Detroit Pistons with the 37th overall pick in the draft. He was also the highest North Texas player to be drafted in the NBA, ahead of [[Kenneth Lyons]] in [[1983 NBA draft|1983]] (47th overall).<ref name=UNTDRAFT/> On July 19, 2013, he signed with the Pistons.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/pistons/news/detroit-pistons-sign-draft-selections-kentavious-caldwell-pope-and-tony-mitchell|title=Detroit Pistons Sign Draft Selections Kentavious Caldwell-Pope and Tony Mitchell|date=July 19, 2013|work=NBA.com|access-date=September 25, 2015}}</ref> When the 2013 rookie class convened for its annual photo shoot and filled out its NBA.com Rookie Survey, the class voted Mitchell as the most athletic.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/2013/news/features/john_schuhmann/08/26/2013-14-nba-rookie-survey/index.html|title=Magic's Oladipo among rookie favorites to stand out in 2013-14|access-date=October 15, 2013|date=August 26, 2013|author=Schuhmann, John|work=[[NBA.com]]}}</ref>

On December 26, 2013, Mitchell was assigned to the Fort Wayne Mad Ants.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=14979|title=Detroit Pistons assign Tony Mitchell and Peyton Siva to D-League|date=December 26, 2013|work=InsideHoops.com|access-date=September 25, 2015}}</ref> On January 13, 2014, he was recalled by the Pistons.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=15069|title=Detroit Pistons recall Peyton Siva and Tony Mitchell from D-League|date=January 13, 2014|work=InsideHoops.com|access-date=September 25, 2015}}</ref> On January 31, 2014, he was reassigned to the Mad Ants.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/pistons/news/pistons-re-assign-peyton-siva-and-tony-mitchell-ft-wayne-mad-ants|title=Pistons Re-Assign Peyton Siva and Tony Mitchell to Ft. Wayne Mad Ants|date=January 31, 2014|work=NBA.com|access-date=September 25, 2015}}</ref> He was later recalled in February 2014. While not making an appearance for the Pistons in the 2014–15 season, Mitchell was assigned multiple times to the [[Grand Rapids Drive]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://dleague.nba.com/news/assignments/ |title=2014-15 NBA Assignments |work=NBA.com |access-date=September 25, 2015 |url-status=unfit |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150628235947/http://dleague.nba.com/news/assignments/ |archive-date=June 28, 2015 }}</ref>

===Short stint with Phoenix Suns (2014–2015)===
On December 24, 2014, he was traded to the [[Phoenix Suns]] in exchange for [[Anthony Tolliver]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/suns/news/suns-complete-trade-detroit|title=Suns Complete Trade With Detroit|date=December 24, 2014|work=NBA.com|access-date=September 25, 2015}}</ref> However, he was later waived by the Suns on January 9, 2015, before appearing in a game for them.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/suns/press-release/suns-acquire-brandan-wright-celtics|title=Suns Acquire Brandan Wright From Celtics|date=January 9, 2015|work=NBA.com|access-date=September 25, 2015}}</ref>

===Atléticos de San Germán (2015)===
On February 5, 2015, Mitchell signed with [[Atléticos de San Germán]] of Puerto Rico for the 2015 [[Baloncesto Superior Nacional|BSN]] season.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/world/america/151281/tony-mitchell-moves-to-atleticos-de-san-german.html|title=Tony Mitchell moves to Atleticos de San German|date=February 5, 2015|work=Sportando.com|access-date=September 25, 2015}}</ref>

===Cocodrilos de Caracas (2015–2016)===
On September 25, 2015, Mitchell signed with the [[Golden State Warriors]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/warriors/news/warriors-sign-ian-clark-jarell-eddie-tony-mitchell-juwan-staten|title=Warriors Sign Ian Clark, Jarell Eddie, Tony Mitchell & Juwan Staten|date=September 25, 2015|work=NBA.com|access-date=September 25, 2015}}</ref> However, he was waived by the Warriors on October 12.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/warriors/mitchell-waived-20151012|title=Warriors Waive Forward Tony Mitchell|date=October 12, 2015|work=NBA.com|access-date=October 12, 2015}}</ref> On December 11, he signed with [[Cocodrilos de Caracas]] of the [[Liga Profesional de Baloncesto|Venezuelan League]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/world/america/184584/tony-mitchell-signs-with-cocodrilos-de-caracas.html|title=Tony Mitchell signs with Cocodrilos de Caracas|date=December 11, 2015|work=Sportando.com|access-date=December 11, 2015}}</ref>

===Guangxi Rhinos (2016)===
On July 2, 2016, Mitchell signed with the [[Guangxi Rhinos]] of the [[National Basketball League (China)|China NBL]].

===Maccabi Haifa (2016–2017)===
On August 9, 2016, Mitchell signed with Israeli club [[Maccabi Haifa B.C.|Maccabi Haifa]] for the 2016–17 season.<ref>{{cite news|title=Maccabi Hunter Haifa sign former NBA power forward Tony Mitchell for 2016-17 season|url=http://mhbasket.co.il/en/8013/maccabi-hunter-haifa2/maccabi-hunter-haifa-sign-former-nba-power-forward-tony-mitchell-for-2016-17-season/|access-date=September 2, 2016|work=mhbasket.co.il|date=August 9, 2016}}</ref> On February 10, 2017, he was released by Maccabi after appearing in 17 games.<ref>{{cite news|title=Maccabi Hunter Haifa release power forward Tony Mitchell|url=http://mhbasket.co.il/en/8762/maccabi-hunter-haifa2/maccabi-hunter-haifa-release-power-forward-tony-mitchell/|access-date=February 13, 2017|work=mhbasket.co.il|date=February 10, 2017}}</ref>

===Star Hotshots (2017)===
On late February 2017, Mitchell signed with the [[Star Hotshots]] of the [[Philippine Basketball Association]] as the team's import for the [[2017 PBA Commissioner's Cup]].<ref>{{ cite news |last=Dy |first=Richard |title=Star taps ex-Detroit forward Tony Mitchell as Comm's Cup import |url=http://www.foxsportsasia.com/en-ph/news/star-taps-ex-detroit-forward-tony-mitchell-as-comms-cup-import/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170310011829/http://www.foxsportsasia.com/en-ph/news/star-taps-ex-detroit-forward-tony-mitchell-as-comms-cup-import/ |url-status=dead |archive-date=March 10, 2017 |work=[[Fox Sports Asia]] |date=February 28, 2017 |access-date=March 23, 2017 }}</ref>

===Metros de Santiago (2017)===
On May 24, 2017, Mitchell signed with [[Metros de Santiago]] of Dominican Republic for the  2017 [[Liga Nacional de Baloncesto|LNB]] season.<ref>{{cite news|title=Tony Mitchell Jr signs with Metros de Santiago|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/world/america/235259/tony-mitchell-jr-signs-with-metros-de-santiago.html|access-date=May 28, 2017|work=Sportando.com|date=May 24, 2017}}</ref>

===Hapoel Gilboa Galil (2018)===
On February 22, 2018, Mitchell returned for a second stint in Israel, signing with [[Hapoel Gilboa Galil]] for the rest of the season.<ref>{{cite news|title=חוזר ארצה: טוני מיצ'ל מגיע לגן נר|url=http://basket.co.il/news.asp?id=17603|access-date=February 22, 2018|work=basket.co.il|date=February 22, 2018|language=he}}</ref> However, on March 7, 2018, Mitchell was released by Gilboa Galil before appearing in a game for them.<ref>{{cite news|title=הפועל גלבוע/גליל שחררה את טוני מיטשל|url=http://www.one.co.il/Article/308784.html|access-date=March 7, 2018|work=one.co.il|date=March 7, 2018|language=he}}</ref>

===Second stint with Cocodrilos de Caracas (2018)===
On May 8, 2018, Mitchell was reported to have returned and signed with [[Cocodrilos de Caracas]] of the [[Liga Profesional de Baloncesto]] (LPB).<ref>{{cite news|title=Tony Mitchell signs with Cocodrilos de Caracas|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/america/venezuela/273546/tony-mitchell-signs-with-cocodrilos-de-caracas.html|date=May 8, 2018|work=Sportando.basketball|access-date=May 8, 2018}}</ref>

===Fubon Braves (2018–2019)===
On August 4, 2018, Mitchell was reported to have signed with Al Wasl of the [[UAE National Basketball League]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Tony Mitchell (ex Leones SD) joins Al Wasl |url=http://www.asia-basket.com/United-Arab-Emirates/news/542854/Tony-Mitchell-(ex-Leones-SD)-joins-Al-Wasl|date=August 4, 2018|work=Asia-basket.com|access-date=August 4, 2018}}</ref>

===NLEX Road Warriors (2019)===
In April 2019, Mitchell signed with the [[NLEX Road Warriors]] of the [[Philippine Basketball Association]] as the team's import for the [[2019 PBA Commissioner's Cup]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.spin.ph/basketball/pba/tony-mitchell-tapped-nlex-import-for-commissioners-cup-a2437-20190423|title=NLEX Road Warriors bringing in Tony Mitchell for Commissioner's Cup|website=Spin.ph}}</ref>

===Leones de Ponce (2020–2021)===
On September 28, 2020, Mitchell signed with the [[Leones de Ponce (basketball)|Leones de Ponce]] of the [[Baloncesto Superior Nacional]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Ponce adds Mitchell to their roster |url=https://www.latinbasket.com/Puerto-Rico/news/646294/Ponce-adds-Mitchell-to-their-roster |website=Latinbasket |access-date=September 28, 2020 |date=September 28, 2020}}</ref>

===Macau Black Knights (2026)===
On February 19, 2026, Mitchell signed with the [[Macau Black Knights]].<ref>{{cite web |first=Gerry |last=Ramos |url=https://www.spin.ph/basketball/pba/sam-deguara-tony-mitchell-to-reinforce-black-bears-in-pba-stint-a793-20260219 |title=Sam Deguara, Tony Mitchell are imports of PBA guest team Macau |website=Spin.ph |date=February 19, 2026 |access-date=February 20, 2026 }}</ref>

==Personal life==
